Kiln Singebeard was the daughter of a High Ranked Cleric of Moradin and Soldier in the Royal army. She joined the fight on the front lines as a field medic under an old ally of her dad's. Unfortunately many of their platoon were wiped out in an ambush and Kiln was thought lost.

In the days following the ambush Kiln was discovered by a couple of Brunelock dwarves from the southern deserts. They took her with them back to their home to treat Kiln's injuries. The Brunelock couple nursed Kiln back to health and, with some coaxing, taught her their medical knowledge.

Several weeks of  healing, turned into months of recovery, turned into years of study, until the Brunelock dwarves helped Kiln connect to and pact with their god, Osiris the god of Life and Death. Under the Brunelock's tutelage, Kiln became a knowledgeable physician. With Osiris steadying Kiln's hand, she became a skilled surgeon.

After 14 years of living with the Brunelocks, Osiris told Kiln her hands were needed in the far west, across the ocean, in the supposed new world. Today Kiln has arrived in London looking to get passage to the new world by any means necessary.

Her garb is incredibly simple, appearing to be no more than a leather bound vest and a kilt. She carries what looks to be a large needle painted Gold and Blue (Ylkwa). 

Physical appearance
Height:  4' 6"
Weight: 184lbs
Hair: Thick brown hair braided into a mohawk with the sides shaved.
Eyes: While both eyes appear to be green, one is much more vibrant  almost neon green. While the other appears to be a dark and more natural green.

<@403783497564684291>  (Katie) and <@361351593292988425>  (Val)  grew up in and around London. Their family was fairly poor, but they got by. These girls were very close growing up, playing together, getting into mischief, and they have also been known to have long conversations telepathically, thanks to them being kalishtar. Even though they are different people, the same quoir spirit resides in them, making these twin girls quite unique. As they got older their mischief continued, while Amara would play music on her mandolin, Ophelia would sneak around the onlookers and pickpocket their money, jewelry, or anything else of value. Unfortunately for them, they ended up scamming the wrong person one to many times. While Amara was enchanting him with a song, Ophelia stole a pocketwatch that happened to hold some very strong sentimental value. Once he realised what had happened, he became hell bent on trying to get them arrested. After a few close calls with the local authority, they decided it was best to leave London. For them, traveling to Roanoke will give them a fresh start, they’ll be able to start a new life together without worry of being caught and locked up. This way, they can guarantee they will stay together.

When you ask this peculiar, lanky bird his name, he only ever responds ♪; the plucking of a single string on some instrument.
He's made his home in the wild ever since forever as far as he's concerned, and has found strange company in the other unorthodox and monstrous folk that dwell outside of society. Formative years were spent with kobolds, goblins, and even fey, for better or for worse.
But of course that couldn't last. Adventurers, prospective or established, began to frequent the area. When it came to light they were following rumors of an unrivaled archer in the area, it became clear that ♪ drew too much attention for his friends' good.
Even when he left his home region, though, rumors still followed him. So he kept going. And going. And then he hit the ocean. They still hadn't stopped. But, there was good news: a vessel crossing the ocean. He probably stole his ticket, but no one needs to know that. All you need to know is that he's gonna be on this submarine.

Gaffer Fabertell is not so certain of their age and you likely won't be either. There are more stories about the Chronicler than by them and no one, including Fabertell, is altogether certain which are true.
They tend to spend much of their time in quiet observant contemplation and a good deal of what remains of it recording in their leather bound journal. They will never pass up a good story and that likely means being a part of them from time to time.
They are a Kalashtar Warlock though not entirely aware of either of these things. They do know the dream speaks to them and the control some can wield over their dreams they have applied to the waking world as well. To some degree they are convinced this must be the method by which others perform their feats as well. Indeed it is a great mystery that so many seem unaware of this truth and will explain their abilities away via countless other more far-fetched concepts. The simplest explanation being obviously more likely.
Gaffer's storytelling is more a process of investigation than exposition. It is the information they glean that interests more than any entertainment value. However, just as often, the wealthy will pay good money to have their stories written down and it keeps Gaffer only slightly less well off than them.
This is a quick sketch though some could swear their age seems to fluctuate +/- 15 years on any given day and any time spent outdoors will see the addition of a pointed felt hat that any wizened one would envy.

"One ticket to the new world please!" Standing before you is Leaf the goblin. Leaf is a little goblin with a big, albeit crooked smile. She waits for this ship in what appears to be a child's sunday dress she stole off of a clothes line (though she did leave some very pretty flowers in return). With her dark green hair pulled back in braids, Leaf does her best to show that she is civilized, even if she doesn't understand aspects of social society all that well.

"No, no I'm not like other goblins I promise! I'm called by the Wild Mother, see!" She holds up a price of wood with Melora's symbol carved into it,  "Have you heard of her? She's amazing! Ya know, some people say she's abandoned us but I think that if you just listen to all the little critters and leaves," she takes a deep breath and smiles, "you can hear her all around us!"

"Oh this thing?" she looks down at the symbol around her neck, "No I didn't take it! Ya know, it just kind of showed up one morning. Well, the morning after my tribe left me. That night the tree I was hiding under said I didn't have to worry and that everything would be ok. And then when I woke up, poof! It was just there! You can imagine my confusion when I found it, so I tried to find someone who could explain what it meant. After some close calls with a couple of nasty travelers, I found a lovely firbolg who told me that I had heard the voice of the Wild Mother and that I had been blessed. Can you imagine? Me? Blessed?? I didn't believe it either until they showed me how to do some healing stuff. And now I can help people! So if you ever get hurt just let me know, ok?" she smiles through her yellow, jaggedy teeth.

"Oh am I talking to much? Sorry, I haven't spent a whole lot of time in the city, ya know? In the woods you can just talk and talk and talk. The trees don't mind! Anyway, I best be off. I'm really excited about this trip! Who knows, maybe there'll be others like me there!"

Sired into the Cragmail, a small clan of Dwarves nestled in the Scotch Highlands, Karak was shunned due to the lurid circumstances of his birth. As he grew, he began to show proficiency with a hammer and tongs and was begrudgingly taken as an apprentice blacksmith. Much to the chagrin of his master, Karak worked tirelessly to complete his training. He would often forge through the night, experimenting and honing his craft even when not given a task. Soon he had eclipsed what his master could teach him. Karak gathered his few meager possessions and took off into the night. He knew he could not go back home, and now his sights were set on Londontown and failing there, the New World.


Maybe there they will appreciate his work.

She spent her first 11 years of life as an apprentice to her father, The Hunter of Sevenoaks. As the years passed she grew in skill and strength. Wren has grown up with the forest. She is one with the bugs and moss that live on the trees, she knows the animals of the woods and the threats to her and her village. 
The summer before her 12th birthday, upon reaching the honored title that her father held for years, her parents decided to send her to the New World to find a name for herself. Ozgur Tepiderez was born in the seaside village of Raglan, New Zealand. Most of Ozgur's early life was spent lifting things, and moving them from one place to the next, that, and listening to his Tupuna (Grandfather) impart on him and his siblings ominous tales of a dark deal struck by his family's ancient ancestor, condemning them to serve in an endless war after death. But surely, surely these were just stories. Seeing the empty, forlorn look in his father's eyes whenever this story was told taught him otherwise. Growing up, knowing that because of his Natural Strength and Martial prowess he'll be forced to serve as a brutal shocktrooper hellbent on destruction and death. This saddens Ozgur, it truly does. If he thinks about it too long or too much, he gets angry, and enters a deep melancholy. He doesn't like to fight. It is this unresolved inner conflict, this anger that he has held onto for so long that eventually drove him to leave his childhood home, and board a ship, setting off to Britannia. Those next few years of his life were spent working on city docks and the decks of sailing ships, lifting things, and moving them from one place to another. Now Ozgur is set to leave his home once again, to a new world, a world he hopes will bring him some peace. 

Ozgur is a big tiefling man, standing just above 6 foot at the shoulder, with even bigger horns, real large texas longhorn-style things that come sweeping out from his head. Some narrow doorways have proven to be an issue for him in the past. His yellow eyes appear to burn with anger even when he is at his most relaxed, his skin is rough, and the color of rust, his hair a thick charcoal black, and his trunk-like tail ends in a tuft of bristled black fur. His most striking feature, aside from his horns, are his cloven hooves.

Willow never fit in well with "people." Not the way her family expected her to anyways. She'd rather spend her precious time on this earth, gazing at the clouds in the sky, peering through the treetops and listening to the nearby trickling creek.
Lately, she has become strangely attuned to the terrestrial rhythms. The quick drumming of hummingbird's wings and slow timpani of glacial floes. There is a music all around us if we care to listen and today she heard a call while sitting in the shade of her garden.
Though faint, it seemed to nag and pull away with the ebbs and flows of the tides. Far off beyond the sea is where it begs her to go. She yawns and stretches as she stands.
"Guess I better go see what the fuss is about" She says and she begins to walk in the direction of the call: West towards London.

Background

Web was born into a collective of druids in the sewers of London who followed the circle of spores.  Growing up among other druids who spent most of their days working to maintain the sewer system that keeps London much cleaner than otherwise, they grew accustomed to being a loner, even looked down upon by those above ground. While their work is not glamorous and many scoff at the idea of food grown from rot and decay, Web takes pride in their work, for who else can take literal garbage and feces and make it not only safe to eat, but healthy. They had left their home many times before for trips to other druidic circles, and especially throughout the city of London. When they reached 18, however, they decided that it was time to make it on their own. Having heard of this new land across the sea, they decided that it would be an excellent way to learn how to build a community and discover more about the wider world.

Appearance

Web is a medium humanoid figure, who tends to cover up their entire body when with strangers. The irises of their eyes are a bright, almost lime green, while their skin is a more muted greenish tan, similar to some types of elf or orc. Most of their body is covered in a thin layer of coarse black hair, though their head hair is slightly longer and lighter. Their ears are pointed, like that of an elf. They wear a black cloak with streaks of green on it, which are intended to invoke the spirit of the species of spider they associate themselves with.

Personality

Web does not necessarily wish to avoid interaction with others, and in fact has left their home precisely to seek companionship. However, they are quite reserved and wish to understand things about people they may befriend. They have an unusual relationship with death, and believe that it is in fact an act of honoring the deceased to raise them as undead.

Web is non-binary and uses they/them pronouns.

Alane never liked home. For many people, a life spent farming of mining in the Highlands is perfect; low risk, low reward, not being a target and raising a family in peace. But Alane wanted more; he wanted to see the world. So he went from York to Copenhagen to Milan before settling in Vienna, finding work as a strongman due to his natural physical prowess. He rose through the ranks, learning of high ranking criminals and the people who held bounties for their heads. He took opportunities as they came, taking out friends and enemies alike to earn his gold. But a life spent killing the only people you know gets to you, and makes the people that they knew hate you for doing what you did. So Alane sought a place where nobody had heard his name. Where nobody had heard of the horrors he committed. Where nobody hated him. He made his way to London, hearing of the coming expeditions to the new lands of the West, hoping to make himself a name that people didn't spit at when they heard it.

Alane is a half-orc, standing tall at 6'5" and an extremely burly physique born from spending a life beating people up in alleys. His clothes are nothing special; a cloth tunic under a jacket with some loose trousers and sturdy leather boots. He has a beard that is obviously not there because Alane wants it to be, but because he cannot be bothered to get rid of it. He carries 2 short swords at his belt.
